content.text: Section 28 is the only governing-law/forum provision in the document; there is no arbitration clause, no offshore seat, and no Order Form carve-out permitting different law (§ 2.2 precedence does not override it).

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.
input.rationale: § 28 sits at our preferred position, not merely the fallback. § 28.1 makes New York law the governing law of the Agreement and of each dispute arising from it (with CISG expressly disapplied), and § 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts located in New York County, with both Parties irrevocably submitting to personal jurisdiction and waiving venue and inconvenient-forum objections. There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document, so no question of a foreign seat arises, and despite Brightline being a UK entity there is no English or other non-accepted law or venue; § 2.2's precedence ladder lets an Order Form vary only a provision it expressly identifies, and no exhibit supplies a competing forum. The § 28.2 carve-out permitting either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction is a standard mutual reservation that preserves our own ability to protect our data and IP quickly, and it does not displace the exclusive New York forum for the merits. The § 28.3 pre-filing executive-escalation step is likewise mutual, capped at fifteen business days, and expressly does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period, so it is not a barrier to court access. No redline required.
